active_themes.label: Talks Over Tankers
active_themes.summary: Day 142: diesel hit a fresh record high on the combined effect of the Iran war and Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries, and Israel struck southern Lebanon after a Hezbollah drone launch — a fresh escalation on top of an already-elevated conflict. The energy cost pressure this generates is now feeding directly into the Fed's dilemma: it can't cut into an economy with record diesel prices without risking a fresh inflation leg.

active_themes.label: AI Trade Loses Its Shield
active_themes.summary: Day 94: on today's broad down day, the Nasdaq (-0.29%) again outperformed the Dow (-0.51%) and S&P (-0.38%), extending the pattern break first seen on yesterday's up day. Two consecutive sessions of tech resilience — one up, one down — is a real signal worth tracking, but it's not yet proof the yield-sensitivity that hurt growth stocks all summer has genuinely eased.

active_themes.label: The Fix Unwound
active_themes.summary: Day 112: the jobs report reversed the late-session calm from the prior day, pushing yields back up as strong labor data undercuts the case for near-term cuts. UK swap rates remain near three-year highs and the Bank of England's chief economist is still pushing a hawkish line, so the global bond-market pressure has not eased — it just paused for a session.

active_themes.label: Fed Voices Split
active_themes.summary: Day 142: Trump publicly demanded rate cuts within hours of a stronger-than-expected jobs report, putting direct political pressure on Kevin Warsh precisely when the data argues for holding steady. The Bank of England's own chief flagged the broader pattern — populist pressure on central bank independence — showing this isn't isolated to the Fed. The open question remains whether Warsh's actual policy language bends toward the political pressure or holds to the data.

open_watchlist.meaning: That would mark a real shift in the committee's center of gravity toward hikes, not just individual officials talking tough.

open_watchlist.condition: The next long-term Treasury or UK gilt auction shows strong demand and a lower yield, versus another weak print.
open_watchlist.meaning: A strong auction would say investors still want long-term government debt at these rates; a weak one confirms the sell-off is a demand problem, not just an oil scare.

open_watchlist.condition: The Nasdaq underperforms the Dow again on the next day markets broadly rise, not just fall.
open_watchlist.meaning: A second up-day gap would confirm this is a yield-driven repricing of growth stocks, not ordinary risk-off noise.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether another Fed official — hawk or dove — publicly echoes Waller's conditional hold language in the coming sessions.
open_watchlist.meaning: If Waller stays a lone voice, the hawkish Barr/Warsh line remains the Fed's dominant signal and today's rally is more relief than reversal.

open_watchlist.condition: Nasdaq's performance versus the Dow on the next broad up day for stocks.
open_watchlist.meaning: A repeat of today's Nasdaq outperformance would suggest the yield-driven pressure on AI and growth valuations is genuinely easing, not just paused for one session.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether Brent crude holds today's late pullback or reverses back toward its recent highs over the next several sessions.
open_watchlist.meaning: A sustained retreat lets bond yields keep cooling; a reversal higher puts the inflation-and-rates story right back in the driver's seat.

open_watchlist.meaning: Would signal the Fed's independence is bending to political pressure, a much bigger deal than any single rate decision.

open_watchlist.meaning: Would tighten the Fed's bind further — strong jobs plus rising energy costs makes any rate cut look riskier.
